lessons.title: Letter Shift (Caesar-style) Coding
lessons.concept: In letter shift coding, each letter in a word is replaced by another letter a fixed number of positions forward or backward in the alphabet. To decode, identify the consistent shift applied to all letters and reverse it.
lessons.formula: If coded letter = original letter shifted by +k positions (wrapping A-Z), then decoded letter = coded letter shifted by -k positions.
lessons.worked_example: If CAT is coded as FDW, observe C->F (+3), A->D (+3), T->W (+3). So shift is +3. To code DOG with +3: D->G, O->R, G->J, giving GRJ.
mistakes: Assuming the same shift without checking all letters
Forgetting to wrap around the alphabet (e.g., after Z comes A when shifting forward)
Confusing forward and backward shifts when decoding

lessons.title: Letter-Number and Positional Mapping
lessons.concept: Sometimes letters are coded using their alphabetical positions (A=1, B=2, ..., Z=26) or by reversing positions (A=26, B=25, ..., Z=1, also called opposite letters). Recognizing these mappings helps solve coding-decoding questions quickly.
lessons.formula: Forward position: A=1 to Z=26. Opposite letter position: A<->Z, B<->Y, etc., value = 27 - forward position.
lessons.worked_example: If B=2 and D=4 in a simple positional code, the word BAD is 2,1,4. If using opposite letters, A becomes Z, B becomes Y, C becomes X.
mistakes: Mixing up forward positions with opposite-letter mapping
Off-by-one errors when counting letter positions
Applying number mapping to some letters and shift mapping to others inconsistently

lessons.title: Pattern and Substitution Coding
lessons.concept: Some codes follow patterns such as reversing the word, rearranging letters, or substituting letters based on a fixed but non-uniform mapping shown in examples. The key is to infer the exact rule from the given example(s) and apply it consistently.
lessons.formula: Infer rule from example: identify transformation per letter/position -> apply same transformation to target word.
lessons.worked_example: If 'ROAD' is coded as 'DAOR' (letters reversed), then 'BOOK' coded by the same rule becomes 'KOOB'.
mistakes: Guessing a rule from one letter without verifying it on the whole word
Applying reversal or rearrangement in the wrong order
Overlooking that a different example implies a different rule

practice.question: If each letter is shifted forward by 2 positions (A->C, B->D, ..., Y->A, Z->B), how is 'CAT' coded?
practice.explanation: Shift each letter forward by 2: C->E, A->C, T->V. So CAT becomes ECV.

practice.question: In a certain code, 'DOG' is written as 'FQI'. How is 'CAT' written in the same code?
practice.explanation: D(4)->F(6), O(15)->Q(17), G(7)->I(9): each letter is shifted forward by 2. Apply to CAT: C->E, A->C, T->V, giving ECV.

practice.question: In a certain code, 'STOP' is written as 'POTS'. Using the same rule, how is 'TIME' written?
practice.explanation: STOP reversed is POTS, so the rule is to reverse the letters of the word. TIME reversed is EMIT.

practice.question: If 'BALL' is coded as 'ABKK' by shifting each letter backward by 1 position, how is 'GAME' coded in the same way?
practice.explanation: Shift each letter backward by 1: G->F, A->Z (wrap around), M->L, E->D. So GAME becomes FZLD.

questions.question: If in a certain code 'PEN' is written as 'QFO', how is 'INK' written in that code?
questions.explanation: P->Q, E->F, N->O: each letter shifts forward by 1. Apply to INK: I->J, N->O, K->L, giving JOL.

questions.question: If letters are assigned numbers A=1 to Z=26, what is the code for 'FACE' as a sequence of numbers?
questions.explanation: F is 6, A is 1, C is 3, E is 5. So FACE is coded as 6,1,3,5.

questions.question: In a certain code, 'LAMP' is written as 'PMAL'. Which rule is used?

options.C: Each letter replaced by its opposite letter

questions.explanation: Reversing L, A, M, P gives P, M, A, L which matches PMAL. The rule is to reverse the order of letters.

questions.question: If 'MIND' is coded as 'OKPF' (each letter shifted forward by 2), what is the code for 'WORK'?
questions.explanation: Shift each letter of WORK forward by 2: W->Y, O->Q, R->T, K->M. So WORK becomes YQTM.

questions.question: If 'ZEBRA' is coded by shifting each letter backward by 1 (with wrap-around), what is the coded form?
questions.explanation: Shift backward by 1: Z->Y, E->D, B->A, R->Q, A->Z (wrap-around). So ZEBRA becomes YDAQZ.
